name: Angry Face
baseMeaning: Angry face with a frown and furrowed brow.
tldr: 😠 usually says “I’m mildly annoyed,” especially in chats where the problem is small and the relationship is comfortable.

contextMeanings.meaning: 😠 is casual shorthand for mild irritation that does not need a serious explanation.
😠 can express disappointed expectations while leaving the sender’s real complaint partly unsaid.
contextMeanings.example: that’s not what i asked for 😠

contextMeanings.meaning: 😠 can show mild frustration with a date without turning a small annoyance into a full argument.
contextMeanings.example: you left me waiting for 20 minutes 😠

contextMeanings.meaning: 😠 signals that a work mistake annoyed the sender, but it can look informal in a serious professional exchange.
contextMeanings.example: that report still has yesterday’s numbers 😠

platformNotes.note: 😠 fits iMessage’s friend and family conversations, where it can close a small annoyance without sounding like an escalation. It is the mildest option when hotter anger emojis would make the exchange feel bigger than the event.
In Instagram direct messages, 😠 works for mild frustration but can read as a performance of annoyance. A warmer relationship makes it safer; a more polished exchange usually needs words instead.
😠 in Slack can come across as unprofessional because workplace channels demand a more controlled tone. State the correction plainly instead of adding an emoji to a complaint.

WhatsApp commonly carries family and international friend conversations, so 😠 can feel natural there when the issue is genuinely small. It may look slightly more formal than the same emoji in a casual iMessage thread.

generationalNotes.note: Gen Z usually reaches first for 💢, 😤, or 🤬, so 😠 is less their default. Among friends, it still reads as the classic scowl for mild frustration rather than hot anger.
Millennials commonly use 😠 as the standard “I am annoyed” reaction in friend chats. It fits mild frustrations especially well, while 😡 carries more heat.
Gen X also treats 😠 as a default expression of irritation. Its straightforward scowl can feel natural with friends and mid-tier acquaintances, but too casual for many work exchanges.

warnings.title: Too mild for a serious offense
warnings.description: After a major betrayal or serious failure, 😠 can make the sender seem as though they are only performing anger. Use plain language or a stronger angry emoji such as 😡 when the feeling is genuinely hot.

warnings.title: Too casual for formal work
warnings.description: A 😠 sent to a boss, parent, or formal coworker can seem disrespectful or insubordinate. Explain the problem directly without the emoji.

seoDescription: What does 😠 mean? It usually signals mild annoyance or soft frustration, not serious rage, and its effect depends on the message, relationship, and platform.

longForm.overview:
😠 joined Unicode 6.0 in 2010 as a straightforward digital scowl: the early version of saying “I’m angry.” As emoji use became more conversational, that literal anger softened into something more useful. Today it usually marks a small annoyance—the missed detail, minor inconvenience, or slightly off message—without claiming that the relationship is in danger. That softening is the key change: 😠 lets someone show annoyance without starting an argument.

It is also the mildest of the frown faces. Its face is yellow on most platforms, but its furrowed brow remains unmistakably angry; 😡 looks hotter because it is red and pouting. That difference matters: 😠 fits the small slip, 😡 fits real heat, and 😤 suggests a cartoon huff. If the event is a serious betrayal or major failure, 😠 can seem too tame, as if the sender is merely acting annoyed. Used with a friend or in a warm family thread, it closes a small annoyance neatly. Sent to a boss, a parent, or a formal coworker, it can look careless or disrespectful.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
😠 tends to arrive after a small, concrete irritation: a typo, a wrong order, a coworker’s slightly off message, or a plan that did not happen as expected. In a friend thread, “ugh 😠” says “that was mildly bad” and leaves the recipient room to laugh, apologize, or tease back. It is most useful when the sender wants to vent without turning the moment into a fight.

It also works when the sender feels let down but wants to stay reasonable. “That’s not what I asked for 😠” can communicate “I expected better” while preserving a warmer tone than a long complaint. The same message to a close friend may invite a joke; the same message to a formal colleague may sound like a public rebuke.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 😠 when the event is much bigger than the emoji: a major betrayal, serious screw-up, or genuine fight. At that severity, the face can make the sender appear to be pretending to be angry rather than expressing how angry they are. Use clearer words or a hotter expression such as 😡.

It is also a poor choice in formal work exchanges, particularly with a boss or a colleague whose role makes the relationship more delicate. The same annoyance that feels natural in a family group can read as disrespectful in Slack or email. Write a direct, specific correction there: name the mistake, say what needs fixing, and leave the emoji out.
longForm.howToReply:
Reply in kind when the complaint is small. “ugh 😠” can be answered with “wow 😠” if you made the same mistake, or with “sorry, I fumbled that” if a quick correction is all it takes. In a warm conversation, a joke can work too, provided the sender has clearly used 😠 rather than 😡 or a stronger reaction.

If the issue needs fixing, acknowledge it without dismissing the annoyance: “You’re right, I missed that. I’ll correct it now.” If 😠 appears in a formal work thread or lands after a serious event, slow down and ask what went wrong. If it followed your own content, check whether the frustration was about the details: “Was there a part I got wrong?”

faqs.question: What does 😠 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: Usually that he is mildly annoyed or disappointed, not necessarily that he is intensely angry. The surrounding message and the relationship matter more than the sender’s gender.

faqs.question: Is 😠 ever flirty?
faqs.answer: It is not inherently flirty. Among close friends it can be playful annoyance, but in a dating context it usually points to irritation rather than romance.

faqs.question: Why would someone send 😠 instead of 😡?
faqs.answer: 😠 keeps the reaction controlled and proportional. 😡 communicates hotter anger, so people often save it for a bigger frustration or a moment when they want the emotion to be unmistakable.

faqs.question: Does 😠 mean someone is really mad?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. It often means the sender is bothered but wants to keep the exchange mild; if the underlying problem is serious, 😠 may understate their actual anger.

conversationExamples.message: you sent me the wrong version again 😠
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is mild, familiar frustration rather than a serious accusation. A playful apology or a quick correction will usually close the beat.
The sender is annoyed about a specific mix-up, not necessarily the relationship. Apologize and take responsibility before adding humor.

conversationExamples.message: this draft still has the old client name 😠
conversationExamples.interpretation: The emoji adds frustration to a correctable mistake in a warm coworker conversation. In a formal channel, mention the correction without the emoji.

conversationExamples.message: the delivery app brought the wrong order 😠
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is the everyday annoyance for which 😠 was designed: something irritating, visible, and easy to complain about without starting a fight.

conversationExamples.message: why did nobody save me a seat at the show 😠
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is calling out a small social slight with controlled annoyance. The right response is to acknowledge it, apologize, and keep the tone light if that matches the group.
